messages:
Priya Shah: FYI ACME (org: acme-prod) reports Project Owners can no longer see the Billing tab or create API keys after SSO sync. Console shows a 403 when switching orgs. Repro steps: 1) login 2) switch org -> acme-prod 3) click Billing. Screenshot attached. Customer tried logout/login and incognito, no change.

Alex Chen: Can you paste the network/backend error id or the API response body you saw? Also which flow: SAML or OIDC?

Priya Shah: Error id: err-3b9f2a. OIDC. Backend response for the billing endpoint:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "forbidden",
  "reason": "invalid_audience",
  "message": "token audience mismatch"
}
```
Tried a curl to the API with the same token and got the same 403.

Mateo Ruiz: Hmm, "invalid_audience" suggests the aud claim coming from the IDP doesn't match what our authz checks expect for org-scoped console routes. Did the IdP team roll any mapping changes last night? @idp-bot any deploys noted?

idp-bot: idp-sync: SSO mapping update deployed 2026-03-16T23:42Z. Change: delegated token audience formatting updated (now includes version suffix 'redwood-api/v2'). Rollout: 100%.

Alex Chen: That would explain it — our service expects aud == "redwood-api" for console tokens, not "redwood-api/v2". Quick mitigation: update auth layer to accept both aud values while we coordinate with the IdP team. Can push a canary auth shim to platform in the next ~30m.

Support L2: Workaround to unblock customer immediately: create a short-lived service token for an owner in acme-prod with billing scope and share; or grant a temporary console role via admin API. But we should avoid long-lived manual tokens. Escalating to eng-platform for a targeted fix and to revoke any stale tokens afterwards.

Priya Shah: I'll offer the temporary service token while you deploy the shim. Customer is OK with a short workaround if we can confirm a plan and ETA.

Alex Chen: Deploying canary now to auth-service: will accept aud in {"redwood-api","redwood-api/v2"} for org console routes only, TTL for token refresh set to 0 so users must re-auth. Canary -> 10% traffic in us-east-1.

Mateo Ruiz: After canary is green we'll promote to 100% and trigger a force logout for desktop sessions in the org (to make clients fetch new tokens). I'll also schedule a postmortem and add an alert rule for spikes of "invalid_audience" errors.

Priya Shah: Canary looks green from customer repro at 17:38 UTC — they logged out and back in, billing tab now visible. Confirmed creating an API key succeeds. Customer happy for now.

Support L2: Follow-ups: 1) coordinate with IdP team to agree on canonical aud format and roll back or standardize mapping; 2) add unit/integration tests for aud variants; 3) monitor for any other orgs affected.

Mateo Ruiz: I'll draft the postmortem and the policy for preflight checks when IdP mapping changes are deployed. Also adding a runbook step: if invalid_audience spikes, check idp-sync changelog and consider a canary auth update.

Priya Shah: Thanks all — customer confirmed resolution at 17:40 UTC. Will close once postmortem link is posted. :tada:
